title: Francisco Lindor expected to return for Mets this month, could impact trade deadline plans
content:
NEW YORK — Francisco Lindor is expected back at some point this month, New York Mets president of baseball operations David Stearns said Friday. While the exact date remains unknown, the star shortstop’s return holds significant meaning for the Mets’ chances of a turnaround and their direction come the Aug. 3 trade deadline.

It’s hard for the Mets (30-38) to make any real decisions regarding the trade deadline until they get healthy. Despite New York’s poor season so far, the wild-card field is crowded with teams hovering around .500. The Mets were 5 1/2 games behind the third and final wild card entering Friday’s action.

Between now and whenever Lindor returns, the Mets must avoid the kind of poor play that has been synonymous with their season to date. They can’t afford the hole to get too much deeper regardless of Lindor’s presence.

“We want to go as fast as possible as smart as possible,” Stearns said, “and that’s a delicate line.”

Lindor has lingered on the injured list because of a left calf strain since April 23.

Lindor participated in a simulated game of sorts on Friday, facing a minor-league pitcher at Citi Field for at-bats and playing the equivalent of two innings on defense. He has not yet run the bases. Mets manager Carlos Mendoza said the expectation is for Lindor to do more of the same on Monday with an increase in workload. By the end of the week, Mendoza said, the Mets plan to revisit the next steps.

Lindor will likely participate in a rehab assignment. The simulated work he is doing, however, may decrease the number of minor-league games he needs to play to get ready.

A notoriously slow starter, Lindor, 32, was just getting hot offensively at the time of his injury. His year started with surgery on his left hamate. In 105 plate appearances, he holds a .669 OPS with two home runs and two stolen bases.

The Mets’ lineup is inconsistent. They are missing Lindor, Luis Robert Jr. and Jorge Polanco, who may resume his rehab assignment within the next few days, per Mendoza. New York’s .658 OPS ranks ahead of only the San Diego Padres (.651), which is also the team they’re chasing for the final wild-card spot.

Better health would crowd the depth chart. Without Lindor, Bo Bichette moved from third base to shortstop. Brett Baty has played third base. The Mets originally pegged Baty for a super utility role, but their outfield is solidified with Juan Soto, A.J. Ewing and Carson Benge. At first base, another spot Baty could conceivably play, Jared Young has emerged as a much-needed power threat. Baty’s defense at third base has looked strong, but his bat has lagged; he carries just a .619 OPS with three home runs. If and when Polanco returns, he is expected to serve solely as a designated hitter.
